tag.name: 01.02 GA4 - Ecom Event - Purchase
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `purchase` event when a transaction is completed.

# Use:
Used to track revenue and completed orders in GA4.

# Expected data:
Full ecommerce object including transaction_id, value, currency, items

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "purchase",
  ecommerce: {
    transaction_id: "ORDER-100245",
    value: 64.70,
    currency: "EUR",
    items: [...]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Must fire only once per transaction.
- transaction_id must be unique and must not contain any PII.
- Uses {{GA4 Ecom Base Parameters}} for shared parameters (items, currency, value).
- Depends on additional purchase-specific parameters such as transaction_id, tax, shipping, affiliation, and coupon.
- Validate that value, tax, and shipping are consistently calculated across all purchase events.
- Consider storage-based deduplication (e.g. sessionStorage or localStorage) using transaction_id to prevent duplicate purchase events.

tag.name: 01.11 GA4 - Ecom Event - View Item (Product Page)
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `view_item` event when a product page is viewed.

# Use:
Used to track product detail views.

# Expected data:
ecommerce.items array with a single product

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "view_item",
  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 29.90,
    items: [...]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire on product page load.
- Consider deduplication to prevent duplicate firing on reload or dynamic updates.
- Uses {{GA4 Ecom Base Parameters}} for shared parameters (items, currency, value).

tag.name: 01.12 GA4 - Ecom Event - View Item List

    item_list_id: "category_page",

  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire once per list render.
- Ensure item_list_name and item_list_id are always included for attribution.
- Uses {{DLV - Ecommerce - Latest Items}} for interaction-level item data.

tag.name: 01.09 GA4 - Ecom Event - Select Item

- Helps connect impressions to clicks.

tag.name: 01.05 GA4 - Ecom Event - Begin Checkout
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `begin_checkout` event when a user starts the checkout process.

# Use:
Used to track entry into the checkout funnel.

ecommerce.items array, value, currency

Example:

  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 64.70,
    items: [...]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire once when checkout starts.
- Avoid firing on step reloads or navigation within checkout.
- Uses {{GA4 Ecom Base Parameters}} for shared parameters (items, currency, value).
- Consider deduplication to prevent duplicate firing on reload or checkout refresh.

tag.name: 01.03 GA4 - Ecom Event - Add Payment Info
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `add_payment_info` event when a user selects or submits a payment method.

# Use:
Used to track progress in the checkout funnel and payment method selection.

# Expected data:
ecommerce.payment_type, items, value, currency

Example:

  event: "add_payment_info",
  ecommerce: {
    payment_type: "credit_card",
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 64.70,
    items: [...]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire after payment method is confirmed, not just selected.
- Helps identify drop-off between checkout steps.
- Ensure consistency with begin_checkout and purchase events.
- Uses {{GA4 Ecom Base Parameters}} for shared parameters (items, currency, value).
- Consider deduplication to prevent duplicate firing on reload or checkout refresh.

tag.name: 01.14 GA4 - Ecom Event - Select Promotion
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `select_promotion` event when a user interacts with a promotion.

# Use:
Used to measure engagement with internal promotions and evaluate click-through performance.

# Trigger conditions:
Fires on custom event "select_promotion"

# Expected data:
- promotion_id → String
- promotion_name → String
- creative_name → String
- creative_slot → String
- items → Array (optional, if promotion is tied to products)

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "select_promotion",
  ecommerce: {
    promotion_id: "summer_sale_2025",
    promotion_name: "Summer Sale",
    creative_name: "Homepage Banner v1",
    creative_slot: "homepage_top",
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Uses {{DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion ID}}, {{DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion Name}}, {{DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Name}}, and {{DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Slot}} for promotion attribution.
- Uses {{DLV - Ecommerce - Latest Items}} to capture the most recent interaction.
- Should fire only when a user clicks or taps a promotion.
- Should not fire on promotion visibility (use `view_promotion` for impressions).
- Ensure promotion_id remains consistent across view_promotion and select_promotion events.
- Avoid duplicate firing from rapid clicks or multiple listeners.
- Validate that promotion data matches frontend interaction.

tag.name: 01.15 GA4 - Ecom Event - View Promotion
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends the GA4 `view_promotion` event when a promotion is displayed to the user.

# Use:
Used to measure promotion impressions and evaluate visibility of internal campaigns such as banners, hero sections, and featured placements.

# Trigger conditions:
Fires on custom event "view_promotion"

# Expected data:
- promotion_id → String
- promotion_name → String
- creative_name → String
- creative_slot → String
- items → Array (optional, if promotion is tied to products)

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "view_promotion",
  ecommerce: {
    promotion_id: "summer_sale_2025",
    promotion_name: "Summer Sale",
    creative_name: "Homepage Banner v1",
    creative_slot: "homepage_top",
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Uses {{DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion ID}}, {{DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion Name}}, {{DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Name}}, and {{DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Slot}} for promotion attribution.
- Uses {{DLV - Ecommerce - Latest Items}} for interaction-level item data.
- Should fire when the promotion is visible to the user (not just present in the DOM).
- Should not fire on user interaction (use `select_promotion` for clicks).
- Avoid firing multiple times for the same promotion impression.

variable.name: CJS - Same page referrer
variable.notes:
Detects if the current page load was caused by a browser refresh (reload).

Why this matters:
* Some setups (e.g. WordPress, plugins, or AJAX flows) can trigger duplicate events when the page reloads. This function helps you identify that case so you can block duplicate GTM tags.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Stores the full ecommerce object from the dataLayer.

# Use:
Used as the parent ecommerce object for GA4 ecommerce events such as view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, etc.

# Expected data:
Object

Example:
{
  currency: "EUR",
  value: 129.90,
  items: [...],
  transaction_id: "12345"
}

# Notes:
This variable should return the complete ecommerce payload exactly as pushed to the dataLayer.
Dependent child variables may extract individual keys from this object.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Affiliation Code
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the affiliation value from the ecommerce object.

# Use:
Used to identify the store, sales channel, or partner associated with the transaction.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"vaikuttaja martti"

# Notes:
Typically used in purchase events.
Maps to ecommerce.affiliation or equivalent key.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Coupon
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the coupon or promo code applied to the ecommerce event.

# Use:
Used in GA4 ecommerce tracking to measure discount usage.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"SUMMER10"

# Notes:
Can exist at event level or item level depending on implementation.
Confirm source structure in the dataLayer.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Currency Code
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the currency used in the ecommerce event.

# Use:
Ensures revenue and value are attributed to the correct currency in GA4.

# Expected data:
String (ISO 4217 format)

Example:
"EUR"

# Notes:
Should be consistent across all ecommerce events.
Typically maps to ecommerce.currency.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Items
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the items array from the ecommerce object.

# Use:
Used in GA4 ecommerce events to send product-level data.

# Expected data:
Array of objects

Example:
[
  {
    item_id: "SKU_12345",
      item_name: "Stan and Friends Tee",
      affiliation: "Google Merchandise Store",
      coupon: "SUMMER_FUN",
      discount: 2.22,
      index: 0,
      item_brand: "Google",
      item_category: "Apparel",
      item_category2: "Adult",
      item_category3: "Shirts",
      item_category4: "Crew",
      item_category5: "Short sleeve",
      item_list_id: "related_products",
      item_list_name: "Related Products",
      item_variant: "green",
      location_id: "ChIJIQBpAG2ahYAR_6128GcTUEo",
      price: 10.01,
      google_business_vertical: "retail",
      quantity: 3
  }
]

# Notes:
Core ecommerce variable.
Should return the full items array without modification.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Latest Items
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the most recent ecommerce items array available.

# Use:
Used when item data needs to persist beyond the original ecommerce event.

# Expected data:
Array of objects

Example:
Latest items from the most recent ecommerce interaction.

# Notes:
This appears to be a custom variable.
Confirm how and when it is populated.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Payment Type
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the selected payment method.

# Use:
Used in checkout and purchase tracking.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"credit_card"

# Notes:
Typically used in add_payment_info or purchase events.
Maps to ecommerce.payment_type or equivalent key.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Shipping Cost
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the shipping cost for the transaction.

# Use:
Used in purchase tracking to separate shipping from product revenue.

# Expected data:
Number

Example:
4.90

# Notes:
Should not include currency symbols.
Typically maps to ecommerce.shipping.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Shipping Tier
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the selected shipping method or tier.

# Use:
Used in checkout tracking.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"Express" or "Toimitus kotiin"

# Notes:
Typically used in add_shipping_info events.
Maps to ecommerce.shipping_tier or equivalent key.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Tax
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the tax amount for the transaction.

# Use:
Used in purchase tracking to separate tax from revenue.

# Expected data:
Number

Example:
24.80

# Notes:
Should not include currency symbols.
Typically maps to ecommerce.tax.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Transaction ID (Order ID)
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the unique transaction or order ID.

# Use:
Used in purchase tracking and deduplication.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"ORDER-100245"

# Notes:
- Must be unique per transaction.
- Critical for avoiding duplicate purchase tracking.

- Must not contain any personally identifiable information (PII), 
-- Email addresses
-- Names 
-- Phone numbers
-- Customer IDs that can be traced back to an individual.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Value
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the total value of the ecommerce event.

# Use:
Used in GA4 for revenue and event value reporting.

# Expected data:
Number

Example:
129.90

# Notes:
Should not include currency symbols.
Confirm whether this includes shipping and tax.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Item List Name
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Identifies the name of the product list where the item was shown.

# Use:
Used in GA4 to attribute impressions, clicks, and conversions to a specific list.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"Search Results"
"Category Page - T-Shirts"
"Homepage Recommendations"

# Notes:
Should be human-readable and consistent across the site.
Used for reporting and analysis in GA4 (e.g. which lists drive engagement).
Avoid using dynamic or overly granular values that fragment reporting.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Item List ID
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Provides a stable identifier for the product list.

# Use:
Used in GA4 to group and standardize list tracking across different pages or contexts.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"search_results"
"category_tshirts"
"homepage_recommendations"

# Notes:
Should be consistent and machine-friendly (no spaces, lowercase recommended).
Acts as a stable key even if item_list_name changes.
Useful for maintaining clean reporting over time.

variable.name: GA4 Ecom Base Parameters
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Defines the base ecommerce parameters shared across GA4 ecommerce events.

# Use:
Used as a reusable configuration for GA4 event tags to ensure consistent parameter mapping.

# Expected data:
- items → Array of product objects
- currency → String (ISO 4217 format)
- value → Number

Example:
{
  items: [...],
  currency: "EUR",
  value: 129.90
}

# Notes:
- Centralizes common ecommerce parameters to avoid duplication across tags.
- Ensures consistent data structure for GA4 ecommerce reporting.
- Depends on the following variables:
  - {{DLV - Ecommerce - Items}}
  - {{DLV - Ecommerce - Currency Code}}
  - {{DLV - Ecommerce - Value}}
- Should be used in all ecommerce-related GA4 event tags (e.g. view_item, add_to_cart, purchase).
- Confirm that value consistently includes or excludes shipping and tax across all events.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion Name
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the name of the promotion associated with a product or ecommerce interaction.

# Use:
Used in GA4 to attribute user interactions and conversions to specific promotions (e.g. banners, campaigns, internal offers).

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"Summer Sale Banner"
"Black Friday 2025"
"Homepage Hero Promo"

# Notes:
- Should clearly describe the promotion in a human-readable format.
- Must be consistent across all events where the same promotion appears.
- Typically used together with promotion_id for stable tracking.
- Ensure alignment between promotion_name and promotion_id to avoid fragmented reporting.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Promotion ID
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the unique identifier of the promotion associated with a product or ecommerce interaction.

# Use:
Used in GA4 to consistently track and group promotion performance across events and sessions.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"summer_sale_2025"
"bf_2025_hero_banner"
"homepage_promo_01"

# Notes:
- Should be stable and consistent across all events where the same promotion appears.
- Use a machine-friendly format (lowercase, no spaces, underscores recommended).
- Acts as the primary key for promotion tracking, even if promotion_name changes.
- Typically used together with promotion_name for readable reporting.
- Ensure naming conventions are standardized across all promotions.

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Name
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the name of the creative used in the promotion (e.g. banner, image, or variation).

# Use:
Used in GA4 to differentiate between different creatives within the same promotion.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"Homepage Banner v1"
"Red CTA Variant"
"Hero Image - Summer Sale"

# Notes:
- Should describe the visual or variant of the promotion.
- Useful for A/B testing and comparing creative performance.
- Should be consistent across events for the same creative.
- Typically used together with promotion_id and promotion_name.
- Avoid overly dynamic values that fragment reporting.
- Should not contain any personally identifiable information (PII).

variable.name: DLV - Ecommerce - Creative Slot
variable.notes:
# Purpose:
Captures the placement or location of the promotion on the page.

# Use:
Used in GA4 to analyze performance based on where the promotion is displayed.

# Expected data:
String

Example:
"homepage_top"
"category_sidebar"
"product_page_banner"
"checkout_cross_sell"

# Notes:
- Should describe the position of the promotion in a consistent, machine-friendly format.
- Helps identify which placements drive the most engagement and conversions.
- Should remain stable across sessions and pages.
- Typically used together with promotion_id and creative_name.
- Use lowercase and underscores for consistency.
- Should not contain any personally identifiable information (PII).
